bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties

title.zh: 卷三十二 死節傳第二十: 王彥章
title.en: Volume 32 Biographies of Martyrs to Virtue 12: Wang Yanzhang
title.raw: 卷三十二 死節傳第二十: 王彥章 Volume 32 Biographies of Martyrs to Virtue 12: Wang Yanzhang

sentences.zh: 語曰：「世亂識忠臣。

translations.literal: The saying goes: "In a chaotic age one knows loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says: "In chaos, loyal ministers stand revealed.

sentences.zh: 」誠哉！

translations.literal: " How true!
translations.idiomatic: " How true that is!

sentences.zh: 五代之際，不可以為無人，吾得全節之士三人焉，作《死節傳》。

translations.literal: In the age of the Five Dynasties one cannot say there were no men of worth. I have found three who kept their integrity whole, and compose this "Biography of Martyrs to Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The Five Dynasties were not without men of worth. I have found three who died with their integrity intact—and so I write this "Biography of Martyrs to Virtue."

sentences.zh: 王彥章

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhang
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhang

sentences.zh: （裴約 劉仁贍附）〉

translations.literal: (Pei Yue and Liu Renzhan appended)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Pei Yue and Liu Renzhan appended)〉

sentences.zh: 王彥章，字子明，鄆州壽張人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhang, styled Ziming, was a native of Shouzhang in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhang, styled Ziming, came from Shouzhang in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少為軍卒，事梁太祖，為開封府押衙、左親從指揮使、行營先鋒馬軍使。

translations.literal: In youth he was a common soldier. He served Liang Taizu as Kaifeng Intendant escort officer, Left Personal Followers commander, and vanguard cavalry commander on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a common soldier under Liang Taizu, rising to Kaifeng escort officer, commander of the Left Personal Followers, and vanguard cavalry commander on campaign.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，遷濮州刺史，又徙澶州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor acceded, he was moved to prefect of Pu, then transferred to prefect of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor took the throne, he became prefect of Pu, then of Cao.

sentences.zh: 彥章為人驍勇有力，能跣足履棘行百步。

translations.literal: Yanzhang was fierce, brave, and strong; he could walk a hundred paces barefoot over thorns.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang was fierce and strong enough to walk a hundred paces barefoot over thorns.

sentences.zh: 持一鐵槍，騎而馳突，奮疾如飛，而佗人莫能舉也，軍中號王鐵槍。

translations.literal: He carried an iron spear; mounted, he charged and broke through like a gale—yet no other man could lift it. The army called him Wang Iron Spear.
translations.idiomatic: He wielded an iron spear no other man could lift. Mounted, he charged like a gale. The army called him Wang Iron Spear.

sentences.zh: 梁、晉爭天下為勁敵，獨彥章心常輕晉王，謂人曰：「亞次鬥雞小兒耳，何足懼哉！

translations.literal: Liang and Jin were bitter rivals for the realm, yet Yanzhang alone always looked down on the Prince of Jin, telling others: "That second-rank cockfighting boy—what is there to fear!
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Jin were mortal rivals, yet Yanzhang alone always scorned the Prince of Jin. "That second-rate cockfighting brat," he said—"what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 」梁分魏、相六州為兩鎮，懼魏軍不從，遣彥章將五百騎入魏，屯金波亭以虞變。

translations.literal: " Liang split the six prefectures of Wei and Xiang into two commands. Fearing the Wei troops would not obey, they sent Yanzhang with five hundred horsemen into Wei, encamped at Jinbo Pavilion to guard against trouble.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang split Wei and Xiang into two commands. Fearing mutiny among the Wei troops, they sent Yanzhang with five hundred cavalry into Wei and camped at Jinbo Pavilion to watch for trouble.

sentences.zh: 魏軍果亂，夜攻彥章。

translations.literal: The Wei army did rebel and attacked Yanzhang by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army did rebel and attacked Yanzhang by night.

sentences.zh: 彥章南走，魏人降晉。

translations.literal: Yanzhang fled south; the Wei men surrendered to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang fled south; the Wei men went over to Jin.

sentences.zh: 晉軍攻破澶州，虜彥章妻子歸之太原，賜以第宅，供給甚備，間遣使者招彥章，彥章斬其使者以自絕。

translations.literal: The Jin army took Cao Prefecture, carried off Yanzhang’s wife and children to Taiyuan, granted them a mansion, and supplied them generously. From time to time they sent envoys to win Yanzhang over; Yanzhang executed the envoys to cut himself off.
translations.idiomatic: Jin took Cao Prefecture, carried Yanzhang’s family to Taiyuan, gave them a mansion and rich provision, and sent envoys now and then to win him over. Yanzhang killed every envoy and broke for good.

sentences.zh: 然晉人畏彥章之在梁也，必欲招致之，待其妻子愈厚。

translations.literal: Yet the Jin feared Yanzhang while he remained with Liang and were determined to win him; they treated his wife and children all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Jin feared Yanzhang as long as he served Liang and was bent on winning him—they treated his family even more generously.

sentences.zh: 自梁失魏、博，與晉夾河而軍，彥章常為先鋒。

translations.literal: After Liang lost Wei and Bo, its armies faced Jin across the river; Yanzhang was always in the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liang lost Wei and Bo, the two powers faced each other across the Yellow River—and Yanzhang was always in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 遷汝鄭二州防禦使、匡國軍節度使、北面行營副招討使，又徙宣義軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to defender of Ru and Zheng, military governor of the Kuangguo Army, deputy northern campaign commissioner, then transferred to military governor of the Xuanyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to defender of Ru and Zheng, governor of Kuangguo, deputy northern campaign commissioner, then governor of Xuanyi.

sentences.zh: 是時，晉已盡有河北，以鐵鎖斷德勝口，築河南、北為兩城，號「夾寨」。

translations.literal: By then Jin held all of Hebei. They blocked Desheng Crossing with iron chains and built north and south cities on the river—called the "Twin Forts."
translations.idiomatic: By then Jin held all Hebei. They chained off Desheng Crossing and built twin cities north and south of the river—the "Pincer Forts."

sentences.zh: 而梁末帝昏亂，小人趙巖、張漢傑等用事，大臣宿將多被讒間，彥章雖為招討副使，而謀不見用。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor was muddled; petty men Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie held power, and veteran ministers and generals were slandered out of favor. Though Yanzhang was deputy campaign commissioner, his counsel went unused.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor was lost; Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie ran the court, and veteran ministers and generals were slandered aside. Yanzhang was deputy campaign commander, but no one listened.

sentences.zh: 龍德三年夏，晉取鄆州，梁人大恐，宰相敬翔顧事急，以繩內靴中，入見末帝，泣曰：「先帝取天下，不以臣為不肖，所謀無不用。

translations.literal: In summer of Longde year three Jin took Yan Prefecture. Liang was terrified. Chancellor Jing Xiang, seeing affairs desperate, hid a rope in his boot, entered to see the Last Emperor, and wept: "The Founding Emperor took the realm and did not think me unworthy—none of my counsel went unused.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, Longde year three: Jin took Yan Prefecture and Liang panicked. Chancellor Jing Xiang, seeing ruin close, hid a rope in his boot, went before the Last Emperor, and wept: "The Founder took the realm and never thought me unworthy—every plan of mine was used.

sentences.zh: 今強敵未滅，陛下棄忽臣言，臣身不用，不如死！

translations.literal: Now the great foe is not destroyed, yet Your Majesty casts aside my words and will not employ me—I would rather die!
translations.idiomatic: The great enemy still stands, yet Your Majesty ignores me. If I am useless, I would rather die!

sentences.zh: 」乃引繩將自經。

translations.literal: He then drew the rope to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: He drew the rope to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 末帝使人止之，問所欲言。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor sent men to stop him and asked what he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor stopped him and asked what he had to say.

sentences.zh: 翔曰：「事急矣，非彥章不可！

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Affairs are desperate—only Yanzhang will do!
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said: "It is desperate—only Yanzhang can save us!

sentences.zh: 」末帝乃召彥章為招討使，以段凝為副。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor then summoned Yanzhang as campaign commissioner and made Duan Ning his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor summoned Yanzhang as campaign commander and made Duan Ning his deputy.

sentences.zh: 末帝問破敵之期，彥章對曰：「三日。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor asked when the enemy could be broken; Yanzhang answered: "Three days.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor asked when he could break the enemy. Yanzhang said: "Three days.

sentences.zh: 」左右皆失笑。

translations.literal: Those around all burst out laughing.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone around him laughed out loud.

sentences.zh: 彥章受命而出，馳兩日至滑州，置酒大會，陰遣人具舟於楊村，命甲士六百人皆持巨斧，載冶者，具韝炭，乘流而下。

translations.literal: Yanzhang took the commission and rode out. In two days he reached Hua Prefecture, held a great feast, and secretly had boats prepared at Yang Village. Six hundred armored men each carried great axes; smiths came with bellows and charcoal, and all floated downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang took command and rode. Two days later he was at Hua Prefecture, feasting while secretly preparing boats at Yang Village—six hundred armored men with great axes, smiths with bellows and charcoal, all drifting downstream.

sentences.zh: 彥章會飲，酒半，佯起更衣，引精兵數千，沿河以趨德勝。

translations.literal: At the feast, halfway through the wine, he pretended to rise and change clothes, then led several thousand picked troops along the river toward Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-feast he pretended to leave and change clothes, then led several thousand picked troops along the river toward Desheng.

sentences.zh: 舟兵舉鎖燒斷之，因以巨斧斬浮橋，而彥章引兵急擊南城。

translations.literal: The boatmen raised the chains, burned through them, then hewed the floating bridge with great axes; Yanzhang led his troops in a furious assault on the south city.
translations.idiomatic: The boatmen burned through the chains, smashed the floating bridge with great axes, and Yanzhang stormed the south city.

sentences.zh: 浮橋斷，南城遂破，蓋三日矣。

translations.literal: The bridge was severed and the south city fell—it had been three days.
translations.idiomatic: The bridge broke, the south city fell—and it had been three days.

sentences.zh: 是時莊宗在魏，以朱守殷守夾寨，聞彥章為招討使，驚曰：「彥章驍勇，吾嘗避其鋒，非守殷敵也。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was then at Wei; Zhu Shouyin held the Twin Forts. Hearing Yanzhang was campaign commander, he said in alarm: "Yanzhang is fierce—I have always avoided his edge. Shouyin is no match.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was at Wei; Zhu Shouyin held the Twin Forts. Hearing Yanzhang had command, he said in alarm: "Yanzhang is fierce—I have always dodged his spear. Shouyin cannot stand against him.

sentences.zh: 然彥章兵少，利於速戰，必急攻我南城。

translations.literal: Yet Yanzhang’s troops are few; he thrives on speed and will surely strike our south city at once.
translations.idiomatic: But his force is small. He lives by speed—and he will hit our south city at once.

sentences.zh: 」即馳騎救之，行二十里，而得夾寨報者曰：「彥章兵已至。

translations.literal: He immediately galloped to the rescue. Twenty li out a messenger from the Twin Forts reported: "Yanzhang’s army has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped to the rescue. Twenty li out a messenger from the Twin Forts cried: "Yanzhang is here!

sentences.zh: 」比至，而南城破矣。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, the south city had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, the south city was already lost.

sentences.zh: 莊宗徹北城為筏，下楊劉，與彥章俱浮於河，各行一岸，每舟抃相及輒戰，一日數十接。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong dismantled the north city into rafts and floated down to Yang Liu. He and Yanzhang drifted on the river, each on one bank; whenever boats drew near they fought—dozens of clashes in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong broke up the north city into rafts and floated down to Yang Liu. He and Yanzhang raced along opposite banks; whenever a boat came within reach they fought—dozens of clashes in a single day.

sentences.zh: 彥章至楊劉，攻之幾下。

translations.literal: Yanzhang reached Yang Liu and nearly took it.
translations.idiomatic: At Yang Liu Yanzhang nearly broke through.

sentences.zh: 晉人築壘博州東岸，彥章引兵攻之，不克，還擊楊劉，戰敗。

translations.literal: The Jin built fortifications on the east bank of Bo Prefecture. Yanzhang led troops against them but could not take them; he turned back to strike Yang Liu and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Jin raised fortifications east of Bo Prefecture. Yanzhang attacked and failed, turned on Yang Liu, and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 是時，段凝已有異志，與趙巖、張漢傑交通，彥章素剛，憤梁日削，而嫉巖等所為，嘗謂人曰：「俟吾破賊還，誅奸臣以謝天下。

translations.literal: By then Duan Ning already harbored other designs. He trafficked with Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie. Yanzhang was blunt by nature; he raged as Liang shrank daily and hated what Zhao Yan and the rest were doing. He often told others: "Wait until I break the enemy and return—then I will execute the traitors to answer the realm.
translations.idiomatic: By then Duan Ning was already playing a double game, dealing with Zhao Yan and Zhang Hanjie. Yanzhang was blunt; he watched Liang shrink day by day and hated the court’s petty men. He often said: "When I break the enemy and march home, I will kill the traitors and answer the realm.

sentences.zh: 」巖等聞之懼，與凝葉力傾之。

translations.literal: Zhao Yan and the rest heard and were afraid; with Ning they joined forces to bring him down.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan and the rest heard and were terrified; they and Ning united to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 其破南城也，彥章與凝各為捷書以聞，凝遣人告巖等匿彥章書而上己書，末帝初疑其事，已而使者至軍，獨賜勞凝而不及彥章，軍士皆失色。

translations.literal: When the south city fell, Yanzhang and Ning each sent victory reports. Ning had men tell Zhao Yan and the rest to hide Yanzhang’s report and submit his own. At first the Last Emperor doubted; then when the envoy reached the army, rewards went to Ning alone and not to Yanzhang—the soldiers all turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: When the south city fell, Yanzhang and Ning each sent victory dispatches. Ning’s men told Zhao Yan to bury Yanzhang’s report and push Ning’s instead. The Last Emperor doubted at first—then the envoy reached camp and rewards went to Ning alone. The soldiers went white.

sentences.zh: 及楊劉之敗也，凝乃上書言：「彥章使酒輕敵而至於敗。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Yang Liu, Ning memorialized: "Yanzhang drank and despised the enemy, and so was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Liu, Ning wrote: "Yanzhang drank, scorned the enemy, and lost.

sentences.zh: 」趙巖等從中日夜毀之，乃罷彥章，以凝為招討使。

translations.literal: Zhao Yan and the rest slandered him day and night; Yanzhang was removed and Ning made campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan and the rest tore at him day and night. Yanzhang was stripped of command; Ning took his place.

sentences.zh: 彥章馳至京師入見，以笏畫地，自陳勝敗之跡，巖等諷有司劾彥章不恭，勒還第。

translations.literal: Yanzhang galloped to the capital and entered audience. With his tablet he traced the ground, recounting the course of victory and defeat. Zhao Yan and the rest hinted that the authorities should impeach Yanzhang for disrespect and order him back to his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang raced to the capital and laid the battle out on the floor with his tablet. Zhao Yan and the rest had the authorities charge him with disrespect and send him home.

sentences.zh: 唐兵攻兗州，末帝召彥章使守捉東路。

translations.literal: Tang troops attacked Yan Prefecture; the Last Emperor summoned Yanzhang to guard the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: Tang attacked Yan Prefecture; the Last Emperor called Yanzhang to hold the eastern road.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁之勝兵皆屬段凝，京師只有保鑾五百騎，皆新捉募之兵，不可用，乃以屬彥章，而以張漢傑監之。

translations.literal: By then Liang’s best troops all belonged to Duan Ning; the capital had only five hundred Palace Guard cavalry—all newly drafted and useless. These were given to Yanzhang, with Zhang Hanjie to oversee him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang’s best troops were all with Duan Ning. The capital had only five hundred Palace Guard cavalry—raw recruits, good for nothing. These were handed to Yanzhang, with Zhang Hanjie watching over him.

sentences.zh: 彥章至遞坊，以兵少戰敗，退保中都；

translations.literal: Yanzhang reached Difang. Too few to fight, he was beaten and fell back on Zhongdu;
translations.idiomatic: At Difang Yanzhang was too weak to win; he fell back on Zhongdu;

sentences.zh: 又敗，與其牙兵百餘騎死戰。

translations.literal: beaten again, he and a little over a hundred of his personal troops fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: beaten again, he and a little over a hundred of his personal troops fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 唐將夏魯奇素與彥章善，識其語音，曰：「王鐵槍也！

translations.literal: The Tang general Xia Luqi had long been on good terms with Yanzhang and knew his voice. He cried: "Wang Iron Spear!
translations.idiomatic: The Tang general Xia Luqi had served with Yanzhang and knew his voice. He shouted: "Wang Iron Spear!

sentences.zh: 」舉槊刺之，彥章傷重，馬踣，被擒。

translations.literal: He thrust with his spear; Yanzhang was gravely wounded, his horse collapsed, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: He drove his spear into him. Yanzhang was gravely wounded, his horse went down, and he was taken.

sentences.zh: 莊宗見之，曰：「爾常以孺子待我，今日服乎？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong saw him and said: "You always treated me as a stripling—are you satisfied today?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong looked at him and said: "You always called me a stripling—are you satisfied now?

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「爾善戰者，何不守兗州而守中都？

translations.literal: He said again: "They say you are skilled in war—why hold Zhongdu and not Yan Prefecture?
translations.idiomatic: He asked again: "They say you are a master of war—why hold Zhongdu instead of Yan Prefecture?

sentences.zh: 中都無壁壘，何以自固？

translations.literal: Zhongdu has no walls—how could you make yourself secure?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdu has no walls. How could you hold it?

sentences.zh: 」彥章對曰：「大事已去，非人力可為！

translations.literal: " Yanzhang answered: "The great affair is already lost; it is not within human power to mend!
translations.idiomatic: " Yanzhang said: "The cause is lost. No human strength can mend it!

sentences.zh: 」莊宗惻然，賜藥以封其創。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was moved and sent medicine to dress his wound.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was moved and sent medicine to bind his wounds.

sentences.zh: 彥章武人不知書，常為俚語謂人曰：「豹死留皮，人死留名。

translations.literal: Yanzhang was a soldier who did not know books; he often used a common saying: "When the leopard dies it leaves its pelt; when a man dies he leaves his name."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang could not read, but he had a saying: "The leopard dies and leaves its hide; the man dies and leaves his name."

sentences.zh: 」其於忠義，蓋天性也。

translations.literal: In loyalty and righteousness, it was his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and righteousness were in his bones.

sentences.zh: 莊宗愛其驍勇，欲全活之，使人慰諭彥章，彥章謝曰：「臣與陛下血戰十餘年，今兵敗力窮，不死何待？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong admired his fierceness and wished to spare him. He sent men to comfort and persuade Yanzhang. Yanzhang declined: "Your servant fought Your Majesty in blood for more than ten years. Now the army is broken and strength spent—if I do not die, what am I waiting for?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong admired his valor and wanted to save him. He sent men to win him over. Yanzhang refused: "I fought you in blood for more than ten years. Now my army is broken and my strength spent—if I do not die, what am I waiting for?

sentences.zh: 且臣受梁恩，非死不能報，豈有朝事梁而暮事晉，生何面目見天下之人乎！

translations.literal: Moreover I received Liang’s grace; only death can repay it. How could I serve Liang at dawn and Jin at dusk—what face would I have before the men of the realm!
translations.idiomatic: I owe Liang a debt only death can pay. Serve Liang at dawn and Jin at dusk? What face would I show the world!

sentences.zh: 」莊宗又遣明宗往諭之，彥章病創，臥不能起，仰顧明宗，呼其小字曰：「汝非邈佶烈乎？

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong again sent Mingzong to persuade him. Yanzhang’s wounds were grave; he could not rise. He looked up at Mingzong and called him by his childhood name: "Are you not Miaojilie?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong sent Mingzong to persuade him. Yanzhang’s wounds were too grave to rise. He looked up at Mingzong and called his childhood name: "Are you not Miaojilie?

sentences.zh: 我豈茍活者？

translations.literal: Do you think I am a man who clings to life?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you take me for a man who clings to life?"

sentences.zh: 」遂見殺，年六十一。

translations.literal: He was then executed—aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was then killed—sixty-one years old.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖時，追贈彥章太師。

translations.literal: Under Jin Gaozu he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Gaozu he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 與彥章同時有裴約者，潞州之牙將也。

translations.literal: At the same time as Yanzhang there was Pei Yue, a staff officer of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanzhang’s day there was also Pei Yue, a staff officer of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 莊宗以李嗣昭為昭義軍節度使，約以裨將守澤州。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong made Li Sizhao military governor of the Zhaoyi Army; Yue, as a subordinate general, held Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong made Li Sizhao governor of Zhaoyi; Yue, a subordinate commander, held Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭卒，其子繼韜以澤、潞叛降於梁，約召其州人泣而諭曰：「吾事故使二十餘年，見其分財饗士，欲報梁仇，不幸早世。

translations.literal: When Sizhao died, his son Jitao rebelled with Ze and Lu and surrendered to Liang. Yue gathered the people of the prefecture, wept, and addressed them: "I served the former commissioner more than twenty years. I saw him divide spoils and feast his men, wishing to avenge Liang—then he died untimely.
translations.idiomatic: When Sizhao died, his son Jitao rebelled with Ze and Lu and went over to Liang. Yue gathered the people, wept, and said: "I served our old commissioner more than twenty years. I watched him share spoils and feast his men, burning to avenge Liang—then he died too soon.

sentences.zh: 今郎君父喪未葬，違背君親，吾能死於此，不能從以歸梁也！

translations.literal: Now the young master’s father lies unburied, yet he turns against lord and kin. I can die here—I cannot follow him back to Liang!
translations.idiomatic: Now his father is not yet buried, and he turns against lord and kin. I can die here. I will not follow him to Liang!

sentences.zh: 」眾皆感泣。

translations.literal: All were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: All wept.

sentences.zh: 梁遣董璋率兵圍之，約與州人拒守，求救於莊宗。

translations.literal: Liang sent Dong Zhang with troops to besiege the city. Yue and the people of the prefecture held out and sent to Zhuangzong for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Dong Zhang to besiege the city. Yue and the people held out and begged Zhuangzong for help.

sentences.zh: 是時，莊宗方與梁人戰河上，而已建大號，聞繼韜叛降梁，頗有憂色，及聞約獨不叛，喜曰：「吾於繼韜何薄？

translations.literal: At that time Zhuangzong was fighting Liang on the river and had already proclaimed his great title. Hearing Jitao had rebelled and surrendered to Liang, his face clouded; hearing Yue alone had not rebelled, he said with joy: "What did I owe Jitao?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was fighting Liang on the river and had already taken imperial title. Jitao’s defection darkened his face—but hearing Yue alone had held firm, he said with joy: "What did I ever owe Jitao?

sentences.zh: 於約何厚？

translations.literal: What did I owe Yue?
translations.idiomatic: What did I owe Yue?

sentences.zh: 而約能分逆順邪！

translations.literal: Yet Yue can tell loyalty from treason!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yue knows loyalty from treason!

sentences.zh: 」顧符存審曰：「吾不惜澤州與梁，一州易得，約難得也。

translations.literal: He turned to Fu Cunjian and said: "I would not begrudge Ze Prefecture to Liang—a single prefecture is easy to come by; Yue is hard to find.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Fu Cunjian and said: "I would give Liang Ze Prefecture without regret—one prefecture is cheap; Yue is not.

sentences.zh: 爾識機便，為我取約來。

translations.literal: You know how to seize the moment—bring Yue to me.
translations.idiomatic: You know how to read the moment. Bring Yue to me.

sentences.zh: 」存審以五千騎馳至遼州，而梁兵已破澤州，約見殺。

translations.literal: Cunjian galloped with five thousand cavalry to Lia Prefecture, but Liang troops had already broken Ze Prefecture and Yue had been killed.
translations.idiomatic: Cunjian raced with five thousand cavalry to Lia Prefecture—but Liang had already taken Ze and Yue was dead.

sentences.zh: 劉仁贍

translations.literal: Liu Renzhan
translations.idiomatic: Liu Renzhan

sentences.zh: 至周世宗時，又有劉仁贍者焉。

translations.literal: By the time of Later Zhou Shizong there was also Liu Renzhan.
translations.idiomatic: By Shizong’s day there was Liu Renzhan.

sentences.zh: 仁贍字守惠，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Renzhan, styled Shouhui, was a native of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhan, styled Shouhui, came from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 父金，事楊行密，為濠、滁二州刺史，以驍勇知名。

translations.literal: His father Jin served Yang Xingmi as prefect of Hao and Chu and was known for fierceness and bravery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin served Yang Xingmi as prefect of Hao and Chu and was famed for courage.

sentences.zh: 仁贍為將，輕財重士，法令嚴肅，少略通兵書。

translations.literal: As a commander Renzhan was light with wealth and heavy toward his men, strict in law, and had some grasp of military books.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander Renzhan was generous with his purse and loyal to his men, stern in discipline, and had read some military texts.

sentences.zh: 事南唐，為左監門衛將軍、黃袁二州刺史，所至稱治。

translations.literal: He served Southern Tang as Left Gate Guard general and prefect of Huang and Yuan; wherever he went he was praised for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served Southern Tang as Left Gate Guard general and prefect of Huang and Yuan; everywhere he went men praised his rule.

sentences.zh: 李景使掌親軍，以為武昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: Li Jing put him in charge of the personal guard and made him military governor of the Wuchang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing put him in charge of the imperial guard and made him governor of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 周師征淮，先遣李穀攻自壽春，景遣將劉彥貞拒周兵，以仁贍為清淮軍節度使，鎮壽州。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops marched on the Huai, they first sent Li Gu to attack from Shouchun. Jing dispatched General Liu Yanzhen to meet the Zhou army and made Renzhan military governor of the Qinghuai Army, stationed at Shou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou marched on the Huai, Li Gu struck first from Shouchun. Jing sent Liu Yanzhen to meet the Zhou army and made Renzhan governor of Qinghuai, stationed at Shou.

sentences.zh: 李穀退守正陽浮橋，彥貞見周兵之卻，意其怯，急追之。

translations.literal: Li Gu fell back to hold the Zhengyang floating bridge. Yanzhen saw the Zhou army retreat and thought them cowards; he pressed the pursuit hotly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu fell back on the Zhengyang floating bridge. Yanzhen saw the Zhou retreat and took them for cowards; he chased hard.

sentences.zh: 仁贍以為不可，彥貞不聽，仁贍獨按兵城守。

translations.literal: Renzhan thought it unwise; Yanzhen would not listen. Renzhan alone held his troops and guarded the city.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhan said it was folly; Yanzhen would not hear him. Renzhan alone kept his troops in the city.

sentences.zh: 彥貞果敗於正陽。

translations.literal: Yanzhen was indeed defeated at Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen was routed at Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 世宗攻壽州，圍之數重，以方舟載炮，自淝河中流擊其城；

translations.literal: Shizong besieged Shou Prefecture, ring upon ring. He loaded catapults on barges and struck the city from midstream on the Fei River;
translations.idiomatic: Shizong besieged Shou, ring upon ring. He mounted catapults on barges and hammered the walls from midstream on the Fei;

sentences.zh: 又束巨竹數十萬竿，上施版屋，號為「竹龍」，載甲士以攻之，又決其水砦入於淝河。

translations.literal: he also bound hundreds of thousands of great bamboo poles, roofed them with planking, called them "Bamboo Dragons," loaded armored men aboard to attack, and broke the water fortifications to pour into the Fei.
translations.idiomatic: he bound hundreds of thousands of bamboo poles, roofed them with boards into "Bamboo Dragons," loaded armored men to assault the walls, and broke the water fortifications to flood the Fei.

sentences.zh: 攻之百端，自正月至於四月不能下，而歲大暑，霖雨彌旬，周兵營寨水深數尺，淮、淝暴漲，炮舟竹龍皆飄南岸，為景兵所焚，周兵多死。

translations.literal: He tried every method of assault from the first month to the fourth and could not take the city. That year the heat was fierce; rain fell for ten days. Zhou camps stood in water several feet deep; the Huai and Fei surged. The catapult barges and Bamboo Dragons drifted to the south bank and were burned by Jing’s troops; many Zhou soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Every assault failed from the first month to the fourth. Heat hammered the land; rain fell ten days straight. Zhou camps stood knee-deep in water; the Huai and Fei rose in flood. Catapult barges and Bamboo Dragons drifted south and Jing’s men burned them; Zhou dead piled up.

sentences.zh: 世宗東趨濠梁，以李重進為廬、壽都招討使。

translations.literal: Shizong marched east to Hao Bridge and made Li Chongjin overall commander of Lu and Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong marched east to Hao Bridge and made Li Chongjin overall commander of Lu and Shou.

sentences.zh: 景亦遣其元帥齊王景達等列砦紫金山下，為夾道以屬城中。

translations.literal: Jing also sent his commander-in-chief, Prince Qi Jingda, and others to camp below Purple Gold Mountain and build a covered road linking the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent his commander-in-chief Prince Qi Jingda to camp below Purple Gold Mountain and build a covered road into the city.

sentences.zh: 而重進與張永德兩軍相疑不協，仁贍屢請出戰，景達不許，由是憤惋成疾。

translations.literal: Chongjin and Zhang Yongde’s two armies distrusted each other and would not cooperate. Renzhan repeatedly asked to sally forth; Jingda refused—so resentment and grief turned to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjin and Zhang Yongde distrusted each other and would not cooperate. Renzhan begged again and again to sally; Jingda refused—and resentment curdled into sickness.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，世宗復至淮上，盡破紫金山砦，壞其夾道，景兵大敗，諸將往往見擒，而景之守將廣陵馮延魯、光州張紹、舒州周祚、泰州方訥、泗州範再遇等，或走或降，皆不能守，雖景君臣亦皆震懾，奉表稱臣，願割土地、輸貢賦，以效誠款，而仁贍獨堅守，不可下。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Shizong returned to the Huai, broke all the Purple Gold Mountain camps, destroyed the covered road, and routed Jing’s army badly. Generals were taken one after another; Jing’s defending commanders—Guangling’s Feng Yanlu, Guang Prefecture’s Zhang Shao, Shu Prefecture’s Zhou Zuo, Tai Prefecture’s Fang Ne, Si Prefecture’s Fan Zaiyu, and others—fled or surrendered and could not hold their posts. Though Jing, king and ministers alike, were shaken and submitted memorials calling themselves subjects, offering to cede land and pay tribute in proof of loyalty, Renzhan alone held firm and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: First month of the next year Shizong returned to the Huai, smashed the Purple Gold Mountain camps, broke the covered road, and routed Jing’s army. Generals fell one after another; Feng Yanlu of Guangling, Zhang Shao of Guang, Zhou Zuo of Shu, Fang Ne of Tai, Fan Zaiyu of Si—commanders fled or surrendered and could not hold. Jing king and court shook, sent tribute, ceded land, bowed as subjects—Renzhan alone held and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 世宗使景所遣使者孫晟等至城下示之，仁贍子崇諫幸其父病，謀與諸將出降，仁贍立命斬之，監軍使周廷構哭於中門救之，不得，於是士卒皆感泣，願以死守。

translations.literal: Shizong had Jing’s envoy Sun Sheng and others come below the walls to show them. Renzhan’s son Chongjian, taking advantage of his father’s illness, plotted with the generals to surrender. Renzhan immediately ordered him executed. Supervisor Zhou Tinggou wept at the middle gate to save him but could not; the soldiers all wept and vowed to die defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong paraded Jing’s envoy Sun Sheng below the walls. Renzhan’s son Chongjian, seeing his father ill, plotted surrender with the generals. Renzhan ordered him killed on the spot. Supervisor Zhou Tinggou wept at the middle gate in vain; the soldiers wept and swore to die with the city.

sentences.zh: 三月，仁贍病甚，已不知人，其副使孫羽詐為仁贍書，以城降。

translations.literal: In the third month Renzhan’s illness was grave; he no longer knew men. His deputy Sun Yu forged a letter in Renzhan’s name and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Third month: Renzhan was dying and no longer knew anyone. His deputy Sun Yu forged a letter in his name and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 世宗命舁仁贍至帳前，嘆嗟久之，賜以玉帶、御馬，復使入城養疾，是日卒。

translations.literal: Shizong had Renzhan carried before his tent, sighed long, granted him a jade belt and an imperial horse, and sent him back into the city to recover from illness. That day he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had Renzhan carried to his tent, sighed a long while, gave him a jade belt and an imperial horse, and sent him back into the city to recover. He died that day.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「劉仁贍盡忠所事，抗節無虧，前代名臣，幾人可比！

translations.literal: An edict said: "Liu Renzhan gave full loyalty to his lord and held his integrity without stain. Of famous ministers in former ages, how many can compare!
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: "Liu Renzhan gave his lord full loyalty and held his integrity without stain. Of the famed ministers of old, how many can match him!

sentences.zh: 予之南伐，得爾為多。

translations.literal: In my southern campaign, gaining you counted for much.
translations.idiomatic: In my southern campaign, winning you meant more than winning cities.

sentences.zh: 」乃拜仁贍檢校太尉兼中書令、天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: ” He then appointed Renzhan Acting Grand Preceptor of War and Concurrent Central Secretariat Director and Military Governor of Pingyi.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then made Renzhan Acting Grand Preceptor of War, Central Secretariat Director, and Military Governor of Pingyi.

sentences.zh: 仁贍不能受命而卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: Renzhan could not accept the appointment before he died, at the age of fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhan died before he could take up the post. He was fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 世宗遣使吊祭，喪事官給，追封彭城郡王，以其子崇贊為懷州刺史，賜莊宅各一區。

translations.literal: Shizong sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices; funeral expenses were supplied by the state. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng. His son Chongzan was made prefect of Huaizhou, and each was granted an estate.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent envoys to mourn him and pay for the funeral from the treasury. He was posthumously made Prince of Pengcheng; his son Chongzan was named prefect of Huaizhou, and father and son each received an estate.

sentences.zh: 李景聞仁贍卒，亦贈太師。

translations.literal: When Li Jing heard that Renzhan had died, he too posthumously honored him as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing heard Renzhan was dead, he too posthumously made him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 壽州故治壽春，世宗以其難克，遂徙城下蔡，而復其軍曰忠正軍，曰：「吾以旌仁贍之節也。」

translations.literal: Shou Prefecture had formerly been administered from Shouchun. Because Shizong found it hard to capture, he moved the seat to Xiachai and restored the army’s name to the Loyal Upright Army, saying: “I do this to honor Renzhan’s integrity.”
translations.idiomatic: Shou Prefecture had once been governed from Shouchun. Shizong, finding the place hard to take, moved the seat to Xiachai and restored the army’s name to the Loyal Upright Army, saying, “I do this to honor Renzhan’s integrity.”

translations.literal: 【Discussion】
translations.idiomatic: Discussion

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，天下惡梁久矣！

translations.literal: Alas, the world has hated Liang for a long time!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the world has hated Liang for ages!

sentences.zh: 然士之不幸而生其時者，不為之臣可也，其食人之祿者，必死人之事，如彥章者，可謂得其死哉！

translations.literal: Yet for gentlemen unlucky enough to be born in that age, not serving as its ministers would have been enough; but those who ate another man’s salary were bound to die for that man’s cause. A man like Yanzhang may truly be said to have died as he ought!
translations.idiomatic: Yet for scholars born into that age, refusing office would have been enough; but whoever ate a lord’s salary owed that lord his death. Yanzhang may truly be said to have died as he ought.

sentences.zh: 仁贍既殺其子以自明矣，豈有垂死而變節者乎？

translations.literal: Renzhan had already killed his son to prove his loyalty—how could he have changed his colors on his deathbed?
translations.idiomatic: Renzhan had already killed his own son to prove his loyalty—how could he have turned traitor at the point of death?

sentences.zh: 今《周世宗實錄》載仁贍降書，蓋其副使孫羽等所為也。

translations.literal: Now the Veritable Records of Emperor Shizong of Zhou record a surrender letter from Renzhan—but that was the work of his deputy Sun Yu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records of Shizong credit Renzhan with a surrender letter—but that was forged by his deputy Sun Yu and the rest.

sentences.zh: 當世宗時，王環為蜀守秦州，攻之久不下，其力屈而降，世宗頗嗟其忠，然止於為大將軍。

translations.literal: In Shizong’s time Wang Huan held Qin Prefecture for Shu. The siege dragged on without success; when his strength was spent he surrendered. Shizong sighed over his loyalty, yet made him only a Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong, Wang Huan held Qin Prefecture for Shu. The siege wore on without result; when his strength gave out he surrendered. Shizong sighed at his loyalty, yet made him only a Grand General.

sentences.zh: 視世宗待二人之薄厚而考其制書，乃知仁贍非降者也。

translations.literal: Compare how thinly or richly Shizong treated the two men and read the edicts he issued, and you will know Renzhan did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh how differently Shizong treated the two men and read the edicts he wrote, and you will see Renzhan never surrendered.

sentences.zh: 自古忠臣義士之難得也！

translations.literal: From antiquity, loyal ministers and righteous men have been hard to find!
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, loyal ministers and righteous men have been rare indeed!

sentences.zh: 五代之亂，三人者，或出於軍卒，或出於偽國之臣，可勝嘆哉！

translations.literal: In the chaos of the Five Dynasties these three men—some rising from the ranks of common soldiers, some from the courts of false states—how much is there to sigh over!
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos of the Five Dynasties these three—some raised from the ranks, some drawn from the courts of usurper states—how much is there to sigh over!

sentences.zh: 可勝嘆哉！

translations.literal: How much is there to sigh over!
translations.idiomatic: How much is there to sigh over!
